la:verb:trucido.gloss: to slaughter, massacre, cut to pieces, kill in a cruel way
senses: to slaughter, massacre, cut to pieces, kill in a cruel way
la:verb:trucido.html:
trŭcīdo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
perh. for truci-cidare, i. e. truncum caedere
,
to cut to pieces, to slay or kill cruelly, to slaughter, butcher, massacre (class.; syn.: obtrunco, jugulo, perimo).
Lit.: cavete neu capti sicut pecora trucidemini,; cf.: pecus diripi, trucidari, Auct. B. Afr. 20, 6: cives Romanos necandos trucidandosque curavit,: ne hic ibidem ante oculos vestros trucidetur,: trucidando occidere,: quos ferro trucidari oportebat, eos nondum voce vulnero,; : ne pueros coram populo Medea trucidet,: trucidatae legiones,: nobilissum corpus ignobili saevitiā,.—
Transf., to cut up, demolish; to destroy, ruin: seu pisces seu porrum et caepe trucidas,chew up,: haec (nubes) multo si forte umore recepit Ignem, continuo magno clamore trucidat,i. e. extinguishes,: juventus ne effundat patrimonium, ne fenore trucidetur,: plebem fenore,.

la:adj:truncus.html:
truncus, a, um,
adj [root tark-, truc-, to break, tear; cf. torqueo], maimed, mutilated, mangled, dismembered, disfigured, deprived of some of its parts (mostly poet. and perh. not ante-Aug.; syn.: mutilus, mancus).
Lit.: trunca manu pinus regit (Polyphemum),i. e. the trunk of a pinetree,: trunca illa et retorrida manus Mucii,: nemora,i. e. trees stripped of their branches,: truncas mhonesto vulnere nares,: vultus naribus auribusque,: frons,deprived of its horn,; ; : frontem lumina truncam,deprived of its eyes,: bracchia non habuit, truncoque repandus in undas Corpore desiluit,deprived of its limbs,; cf. : puerum trunci corporis in agro Romano natum,: varie ex integris truncos gigni, ex truncis integros,: tela,i.e. broken in pieces,; cf.: trunci enses et fractae hastae,: truncum lignum, i. e. hasta fracta,: membra carmae, Ov M. 11, 560; cf. alnus,without oars,: truncae atque mutilae litterae,: exta,.—
Poet., with gen.: animalia trunca pedum,without feet,: truncus capitis, Sil 10, 311.—
Transf.
Of things, not developed, imperfect, or wanting in their parts: quaedam imperfecta (animalia) suisque Trunca vident numeris,: ranae pedibus,: ipse (nanus) jactabat truncas manus,mdash;
Of members cut off: bracchia,: manus,.—
Trop., maimed, mutilated: (Capua) urbs trunca, sine senatu, sine plebe, sine magistratibus,: pecus,without a leader,: manus vero, sine quibus trunca esset actio ac debilis, vix dici potest, quot motus habeant,: trunca et debilis medicina (sine rerum naturae cognitione), Cels. praef.: sermo (volucrum),: trunca quaedam ex Menandro,fragments,.—Hence, subst.:

senses: an arterial trunk, such as the truncus arteriosus
la:noun:truncus.html:
truncus, i, m.,
the stem, stock, bole, or trunk of a tree (without regard to its branches).
Lit.: cibus ... Per truncos ac per ramos diffunditur omnes,: quid? in arboribus, in quibus non truncus, non rami, non folia sunt denique, nisi, etc.,; cf. ; ; ; ; , ; ; Hor S. 1, 8, 1; ; ; ; ; ; ; .—
Transf.
Of the human body, the trunk, the body, apart from the limbs: status erectus et celsus, nullā mollitiā cervicum: trunco magis toto se ipse moderans,: nemo illum ex trunco corporis spectabat,: recto pugnat se attollere trunco,; cf. : et caput abscisum calido viventeque trunco,: jacet litore truncus. .—
Of a column.
The shaft, —
The cubical trunk of a pedestal, the die or dado, ; cf. Plin. 16, 40, 76, § 201.—
A piece cut off, as a branch of a tree for an our: frondentes,; a piece of flesh for smoking (cf. trunculus),.—
Like caudex, stipes, and the Engl. stock, for blockhead, dunce, dolt: quī potest esse in ejusmodi trunco sapientia?: tamquam truncus atque stipes,. —*
Trop., a trunk, stem: quae (stirpes aegritudinis) ipso trunco everso omnes eligendae (elidendae, Kühn.) sunt,.

la:verb:trunco.gloss: to maim or mutilate by cutting off pieces
senses: to maim or mutilate by cutting off pieces
la:verb:trunco.html:
trunco, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
2. truncus
,
to maim, mutilate, mangle, or shorten by cutting off, to cut off (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose; syn.: mutilo, amputo): truncata simulacra deum,: statuis regis truncatis,: truncat olus foliis,strips, cuts off the leaves,: truncato ex vulneribus corpore,; cf. : truncatā corporis parte, partem corporis,; : cadavera,: caput,: lacertos, Claud. ap. : frontem,i. e. to deprive of an eye,: manibusque truncatus et armis,deprived of his hands and weapons,: quia antiquum illud (signum) vetustate truncatum est,: truncatis arboribus,—Poet., transf.: aquas,to cut apart, rend asunder, separate,: heroos tenores gressu,i. e. to shorten hexameters into pentameters,.—Pregn.: cervos,i. e. to kill,; . —
Trop.: tunc omnibus fere membris erat truncata respublica,.

la:verb:trudo.html:
trūdo, si, sum, 3, v. a.
cf. Sanscr, tard-, to split
,
to thrust, push, shove; to crowd or shove forward; to press on, drive, impel (class.; syn.: pello, expello).
Lit.
In gen.: vis haec quidem hercle est et trahi et trudi simul,: quas mihi tenebras trudis?: trudit et impellit,: adverso trudere monte saxum,: montem pectore,: (hostes) trudunt adversos,: glaciem cum flumina trudunt,: ille hinc trudetur largus lacrimarum foras,: apros in plagas,: ad proelia inertem,: semet in arma,.—
In partic., of growth, to push forth, put forth, send forth (poet.): (pampinus) trudit gemmas,: se de cortice (gemmae),: truditur e sicco radix oleagina ligno,: offenso truditur igne latex, Claud. de Apono, 13.—
Trop.: secundae res laetitiă transvorsum trudere solent a recte consulendo atque intellegendo, Cato ap. : ad mortem trudi,: in quae (comitia) omnibus invitis trudit noster Magnus Auli filium, puts forward (to bring him into office), : quo ne trudamur, di immortales nos admonent,: in vitia alter alterum trudimus,: semel in arma trusos,: truditur dies die, Hor, C. 2, 18, 15, cf.: sic vita truditur, is hurried on, Petr 82: fallacia Alia aliam trudit,presses hard upon, closely follows the other,.

la:noun:trudis.html:
trŭdis, is, f.
trudo
,
a pointed pole, a pike: ferratae,; cf.: trudes hastae sunt cum lunato ferro,.

la:adj:trux.gloss: wild, rough, harsh, savage, fierce, ferocious
senses: wild, rough, harsh, savage, fierce, ferocious
la:adj:trux.html:
trux, ŭcis (abl. usually truci, but truce in ; ), adj.
perh. τρύξ, new, unfermented wine; hence, trop.
,
wild, rough, hard, harsh, savage, fierce, ferocious, grim, stern (mostly poet.; cf.; truculentus, torvus).
Of living beings: horridus ac trux tribunus plebis,: M. Catonem oratorem non solum gravem sed interdum etiam trucem esse scimus,: insectator,: puer,i. e. Achilles,: puellae,i. e. Amazons,: tyrannus,: arietes,: ferae,: aper,: taurus,; 8, 297; 9, 81: Theron,: blattae,ravaging, et saep.—*
With inf.: trux audere,bold, daring,. —
Of things concrete and abstract: (testudo) aspectu truci, Pac. ap. (Trag. Rel. v. 3 Rib.): oculi (draconis), Cic. poët. N. D. 2, 42, 107: vultus,: quemque vocant aliae vultum rigidumque trucemque,: voltu truci,: faciesque truces oculique minaces,: pelagus,: venti,: Eurus, Ov M. 15, 603: classicum,: truci cantu,: sonor,: vox,: herbae tactu,: per lucos vetustā religione truces,: animus,: sententia,: genus dicendi trux atque violentum,: inimicitiae,: eloquentia,: oratio,.—Comp. and sup. given without examples in Rhemn. Palaem. p. 1369 P.— Hence, trŭcĭter, adv., fiercely (late Lat.), .

la:adj:truculentus.html:
trŭcŭlentus, a, um, adj.
trux
,
savage, fierce, ferocious, stern, grim, harsh, cruel, fell (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose; syn.: saevus, crudelis, trux).
Lit.: agrestis, saevus, tristis, parcus, truculentus, tenax,; cf.: quam taeter incedebat! quam truculentus! quam terribilis aspectu,: truculentus atque saevus,; ; ; ; : tigris etiam feris ceteris truculenta,.— Hence, subst.: Trŭcŭlentus, i, m., a play by Plautus, ; .—Comp.: nulla Getis gens est truculentior,: quo truculentior visu foret,: feta truculentior ursa,: Armeniam invasit truculentior quam antea,.—
Of things: truculentis oculis,,

3, 21: aequor,wild, stormy,: vocibus truculentis strepere,wild, tumultuous, mutinous,.—Subst.: trŭcŭlenta, ōrum, fierce conduct or language: truculenta pelagi tulistis,; cf. caeli,: truculenta loquens,.—Sup.: truculentissimum ac nefarium facinus,.—Adv.: trŭcŭlentē or trŭcŭ-lenter, savagely, fiercely, ferociously: nolite truculenter insequi inania verba populorum,; Ven. Fort. Vit. S. .—Comp.: quod truculentius se gereret quam ceteri,: instans,.—Sup.: quam potuit truculentissime eum aspexit,.

la:noun:trucidatio.html:
trŭcīdātĭo, ōnis, f.
trucido
,
a slaughtering, massacring, butchery.
Lit.: inde non jam pugna, sed trucidatio velut pecorum fleri,: civium,.—In plur. absol.: tantas trucidationes facis, Cato ap. .—
Transf., a cutting to pieces, cutting up, cutting off, Cels. praef. med.: arborum,a lopping, trimming,.

la:noun:trulla.html:
trulla, ae, f.dim.
trua
.
Lit., a small ladle, dipper, or scoop (esp. for dipping wine from the crater into the drinking-cups), ; ; ; ; ; . § 20; —
Transf.
A scoop-shaped fire-pan, .—
A mason's trowel, ; .—
= trulleum, a basin, wash-basin, .

la:noun:trutina.html:
trŭtĭna, ae, f.
τρυτάνη
,
a balance, pair of scales (cf.: lanx, statera).
Lit., Müll.; id. ap. : ex trutinis quae staterae dicuntur,.—
Trop.: ad ea probanda quae non aurificis staterā, sed quādam populari trutinā examinantur, * : Romani pensantur eādem Scriptores trutinā,; : aliā parte in trutinā suspendit Homerum,: examenve inprobum in illā castiges trutinā,.
